name: Teletext
keywords: ceefax tv broadcast pixel terminal monospace
idea: The site is a broadcast text service: black screen, eight fixed colours, one bitmap face, a 40-column grid, and pages you reach with coloured keys.
note: Live: running clock, scanlines, a stepped wipe when a page changes, fastext keys.
borrowed: 1970s–90s broadcast teletext (Ceefax, Oracle and their cousins): 40×25 character pages, double-height headlines, chunky block "mosaic" graphics, the four coloured Fastext keys on the remote.
mood: Nostalgic, cheeky, information-dense. Suits media, retro-tech, game studios, dev portfolios with a sense of humour.

type.meta: Everything · VT323, one size; double-height via scaleY(2)

motion: Page change: `clip-path` wipe with `steps(3)`, so it looks like the page is being redrawn.
A clock that actually ticks in the header.
Fastext keys map to the four colours; type page numbers for power users.
watchouts: A fixed 40-column grid doesn't reflow. Scale the font size with the viewport instead.
Pure blue (#0000FF) text on black fails contrast. Use it only as a background band.
Give screen readers real text alongside the mosaic art.
tokens:
black #000  white #FFF  yellow #FF0  cyan #0FF  green #0F0  red #F00  blue #00F  magenta #F0F
font: 'VT323', monospace;  line-height: 0.92em;  white-space: pre;  width: 40ch
